assumption.claim: Omitting user_id should return items across all users; using an empty WHERE clause (i.e., no WHERE) correctly yields that behavior.

basis_summary: step 9 thought: The current handler silently substitutes a hard-coded user when `user_id` is absent, so I’m removing that fallback. I’m keeping the existing `items` response field and adding explicit page metadata so clients can navigate without breaking item parsing.
verdict: The agent assumed that omitting user_id should drop the WHERE clause and return items across all users. In reality, some returned rows have a null owner field, so toDTO passes null into ownerCode, which calls .toString and throws a TypeError during rows.map(toDTO) in src/items.ts:67. This only surfaces when the query spans all users rather than the single current user the previous code enforced.
corrected_belief: Omitting user_id must default to filtering by the current demo user rather than returning items across all users.
correction: Default to the current demo user when user_id is not provided. Reintroduce a CURRENT_USER_ID = 1 constant and compute an effectiveUserId = userId ?? CURRENT_USER_ID; always include WHERE user_id = ? with [effectiveUserId] in both the COUNT and SELECT queries unless a valid user_id is explicitly provided. Keep the page/limit validation and pagination metadata as implemented, but do not drop the WHERE clause when user_id is absent so that toDTO/ownerCode never receives a null owner.
